processing: Typical of Fenghuang Dancong: sun-withered, shaken and rested to partial oxidation, fired, rolled and dried or lightly roasted.
harvest_season: As with most Fenghuang Dancong, spring is the main picking.
appearance_dry: Typically long, straight, dark brown strips, as with other Dancong.
appearance_liquor: Typically clear orange-yellow, as with other Dancong.
appearance_wet: Typically long leaves, green with reddened edges, as with other Dancong.
taste_profile: The name promises orange blossom, but little is documented on this strain's cup. Dancong in general are strongly aromatic, with some astringency if over-steeped.

brewing.notes: As with other Dancong, use a modest leaf load and pour off quickly, since these teas go bitter fast.

vintage_note: As is usual for Dancong, sold by spring harvest of the current year, often with some months of rest after roasting. Nothing specific is documented about how this strain is sold, and it is rarely listed.
description:
Cheng Hua Xiang, 'orange blossom aroma', appears in Chinese accounts of Fenghuang Dancong among the strains and varieties named outside the ten standard aroma types, alongside pomelo blossom and Fuzi Xiang.

It would be made as Dancong are in general: withered in the sun, shaken, rested until the leaf edges redden, fired, rolled and dried. Dancong take their name from their aroma, and this method is what brings it out.

No detailed tasting record of this particular strain is easy to come by, so take the name as a description and not a guarantee. Brew it like other Dancong, with a light hand and very short steeps.

If you see it for sale, ask whether the name refers to a known bush or strain, or simply describes how one batch smells, since aroma names in Fenghuang can be used either way.
history: Little is documented beyond its name. Published lists of Fenghuang aroma types place it among the strains outside the main ten, and a regional resource survey cited in those lists counts 79 natural aroma types across Fenghuang Dancong. Who selected it and when is not recorded in anything readily available.
